Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Bangladesh's reply. South Africans are in a huddle near the ropes before they spread out to take their respective positions. It will be Litton Das and Tanzid Hasan to open the innings for Bangladesh. Quinton de Kock has not come out as he is suffering with mild cramps and it will be Heinrich Klaasen with the gloves. Marco Jansen will start with the new ball for South Africa. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, South Africa have a mammoth total on the board and they are on course to topple New Zealand to climb to the second spot in the standings. It will require something special from Bangladesh batters if they are to get over the line here. Can they do the unthinkable or will South Africa cruise to another big victory? Back in a bit to find out.

David Miller is in for a chat. He says that it is a really good wicket to bat on. Adds that he had the job in hand to hit the big ones as he came in with 5 overs left. He adds that the slower ball is sticking on the surface a little. He finishes by saying that he has enjoyed batting alot in his recent form and says that maturity comes with age to understand the strengths about his own batting.

As far as Bangladesh are concerned, they were switched on from ball one, which was visible on the field. They needed a good start with the ball against the strong South African batting unit. It went according to plan for them thanks to early breakthroughs from Shoriful Islam and Mehidy Hasan. In the middle phase, the spinners did well not to leak boundaries, but they were stalled by the gritty stand between Quinton de Kock and Heinrich Klaasen. Having dismissed Markram, Bangladesh had hopes of pulling things back. It wasn't to be as they stood answers to the onslaught from Quinton de Kock, David Miller and Heinrich Klassen. Even after getting rid of de Kock, they failed to wrestle the initiative back and just could not finish strongly with the ball. Mehidy Hasan had only a wicket to his name but he was Bangladesh's most economical bowler on show.

Earlier in the day, it was South Africa's stand-in skipper Aiden Markram who called it right and opted to put runs on the board. South Africa were rocked early with the loss of Reeza Hendricks and Rassie van der Dussen inside the first eight overs. Quinton de Kock and Aiden Markam then got together and laid a solid foundation for their side. Markram took his time initially, but having been there from the start, de Kock made sure not to miss out on loose deliveries. Markram got out on 60, but de Kock carried on and brought up his third hundred of this World Cup. The southpaw went into overdrive after breaching the three-figure mark, and he, along with Heinrich Klaasen, unleashed themselves all around the park. After de Kock's departure, Klaasen continued the blitzkrieg and ensured that at no point did the innings lose steam. Coming in at number 6, David Miller did what he does best and it would have been a dream innings for South Africa had Klaasen not got out on his individual score of 90. Nonetheless, they will be the happier of the two sides at the halfway mark.

South Africa absolutely love batting at the Wankhede Stadium, don't they? 399 against England, and 382 now against Bangladesh. The de Kock-Klaasen show has helped the Proteas post their fourth straight 300-plus total while batting first at this World Cup and their seventh straight 300-plus score while batting first in ODI cricket.
